title: Why does Zotero bibliography change font in Word for Mac? Causes and fixes for 2026
metaTitle: Why does Zotero bibliography change font in Word? Mac fixes
description: Zotero bibliography changing font in Word for Mac? Start with Track Changes, captions and field codes. Here are the fixes that work, in order.
targetKeyword: why does Zotero bibliography change font in Word
intro: Your Zotero bibliography probably changes font in Word for Mac because Word and Zotero disagree about the citation fields. Zotero's own troubleshooting pages name a few likely triggers: Track Changes, citations pasted into image captions, and clipboard tools on macOS. This guide shows how to check each one, in order, without buying anything.
tldr: Zotero stores citations as Word fields, and Refresh rebuilds them.
Turn off Track Changes in Word, then click Refresh in the Zotero toolbar.
Delete any citation inside an image caption. Zotero calls captions the most likely source of the problem.
Press ⌥F9 to see field codes. Press it again to switch back.
Test every fix in a copy. Unlink Citations cannot be undone.

blocks.text: A Zotero bibliography is not plain text. Zotero builds it as a Word field, and it rebuilds that field each time you click Refresh. When the rebuilt text does not match your body text, the font looks wrong. The fix usually lives in the citations, not in the font menu. That is good news, because citations have a short list of causes you can check one at a time.
What the font change looks like on a Mac

The symptom changes from one document to the next. Some writers see the bibliography in a different font than the body text. Others see citations turn into {Citation} placeholders, or see the bibliography stop updating after an edit. Each symptom points to a different part of the chain. Name yours before you change anything.

Click one citation in the body text. If the text around it looks like code, you are looking at field codes, not results. That is a display setting, not damage to your paper. The section on field codes below shows how to switch it back.
What it costs you

The first cost is waiting time. A Zotero forum user on Zotero 7.0.29 with Word for Mac 16.103.1 reported that one citation took about 35 seconds to insert. The dialog spinner sometimes never stopped. That is one person's report, not a measurement. For example, 40 citations at that speed add up to about 23 minutes of waiting before any repair starts.

The second cost is error risk. A 2013 study of 125 master's theses at Tamkang University found that 22.8% of 3,564 references contained errors. That number counts reference errors. It does not measure formatting time, and it does not blame Zotero. It shows only that citation mistakes happen often enough to check before you submit.

The third cost is a rushed deadline. A bibliography that breaks the night before submission forces a choice. You can restore an older copy and lose recent edits, or you can spend the evening on repairs. Both options cost more than a backup copy would have cost you that morning.
Why it happens

Zotero's usage guide does not describe a font setting for the bibliography. Document Preferences lists the citation style, language, footnote or endnote placement, Fields or Bookmarks, and MEDLINE abbreviations. Nothing there controls font. So the practical question is not which font. The useful question is which citation has fallen out of step with the document.

Track Changes is the first suspect. Zotero's troubleshooting page says Track Changes may mark many or all citations as changed. It recommends turning the feature off. On rare occasions, it may make Zotero think a citation is corrupted. A marked citation can look different from its saved state, and the rebuilt text can look wrong.

blocks.title: Fields or Bookmarks?
blocks.text: Zotero's guide says to always choose Fields unless you need to collaborate with colleagues who use LibreOffice. Open Document Preferences from the Zotero toolbar in Word to check which one your paper uses.
Bugs that look like formatting problems

Some reports come from Zotero itself. In a forum thread from November 2025 to January 2026, a user on Zotero 7.0.29 and Word for Mac 16.103.1 turned off Automatically update citations. Every endnote reference then became a {Citation} field. The user reverted to saved versions each time. A Zotero staff member called it a bug tied to the Chicago style's internal ID, with a fix coming in the beta.

Older reports still teach one lesson. A January 2018 thread about Word 16.9 for Mac advised reinstalling the Zotero plugin and restarting Word. That advice is old, and it may not match current Word. Still, a plugin reinstall is a cheap test, so keep it on your list. Check your Zotero version under Zotero > About Zotero. Zotero 10 is the current release on zotero.org.
Fixes you can try today, in order

items: Save a copy. Choose File > Save As and work only in the copy.
Turn off Track Changes. Choose Review > Track Changes and clear it. Then restart Zotero and Word.
Fix the source item in Zotero first. Then click Refresh in the Zotero toolbar in Word. Refresh updates all citations and the bibliography.
Delete citations inside image captions. Then click Refresh again.
Check field codes. Press ⌥F9, or fn+⌥F9 on a compact keyboard. Press it again to switch back.
Restart Zotero and Word. Quit both fully, then open them again.
Reinstall the Word plugin from Zotero, then restart Word.
Find the broken section. In your copy, delete half the document, test, and repeat until the failing part is small.
Unlink only as a last step. Unlink Citations is irreversible, so use it only on a final copy.

blocks.text: Stop at the first step that works. Refresh only after the source item is correct. If a fix makes things worse, close the copy without saving and return to the last clean version. The copy protects you while you test.
How to show or hide field codes in Word for Mac

⌥F9 toggles between field codes and field results in Word for Mac. A Microsoft Q&A answer says to use fn+⌥F9 on compact keyboards. You can also right-click a field and choose the command from the menu. If the shortcut does nothing, open Word > Preferences > View. Uncheck Field codes instead of values. The shortcut flips the same setting.

Turn codes off to see the real result. Leave them off while you check the bibliography font. If you need codes to find a problem, turn them on for that search, then switch them back. Mixing the two views makes it hard to tell what Word actually stores.
Mistakes that make it worse

The risky mistake is working in the original file. Zotero's advice is to copy the document and test in the copy. Writers who skip that step lose the working version when a fix goes wrong. Keep a dated copy each time you finish a fix that works.

The second mistake is clicking Unlink Citations to clean up a broken file. Unlink Citations removes the field codes for good. Your citations stay as plain text, and Zotero can no longer update them. Use it only after the paper is final.

The third mistake is turning off automatic updates to run a test. In the forum thread, that step turned every endnote reference into a {Citation} field. Change one setting at a time, and keep the saved copy open in another window.

The fourth mistake is ignoring captions. Zotero's troubleshooting page says copied citations in image captions are most likely the source of the problem. Search your captions with ⌘F before you blame Word or Zotero.

blocks.title: Unlink Citations cannot be undone
blocks.text: Zotero's guide says removing field codes is irreversible and should usually be done only in a final copy. Save and close your working file before you run it.

blocks.text: Captions, clipboard tools and shared files

Captions cause trouble because people copy citations into them without thinking. Zotero's troubleshooting page says copied citations in image captions are most likely the source of the problem. Check the caption paragraphs for citation text. Delete the citation, then run Refresh. Retype the source as plain text if you still need it.

On a Mac, clipboard tools can also interfere with the plugin. Zotero's troubleshooting page says so directly. If you use a clipboard manager, paste as plain text when you can. That keeps formatting from another app from following the text into your paper.

Shared files add another layer. Agree with co-authors on one editor and one Zotero setup before you start. Check that everyone uses Fields, unless someone in the group uses LibreOffice. A mixed setup makes the bibliography harder to trust, and harder to repair.
Where Lazur helps, and where it does not

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where Track Changes is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to turn it off, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or run other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Word or Zotero. It has no partnership with either app maker. Think of it as a guide that sits beside you while you make each change yourself.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. If your paper holds client, patient or other regulated data, follow your employer's rules before you share a screen with any AI tool. That includes Lazur.
What to do next

Start with the copy. Then check Track Changes, captions and field codes, in that order. Refresh only after the source item is correct in Zotero. If nothing changes, reinstall the plugin, restart both apps, and search the Zotero forum for threads that match your Zotero and Word versions.

Keep a short log. Write down your Zotero version, your Word version, the symptom, and each fix you tried. The log stops you from repeating steps. It also gives anyone who helps you the detail they need to find the cause.

faq.question: Why does my Zotero bibliography change font in Word for Mac after I update?
faq.answer: Zotero's support pages do not name a specific update that changes fonts. Check your version under Zotero > About Zotero. Zotero 10 is the current release on zotero.org, so update first, then run Refresh and check the bibliography again.

faq.question: Can I change the bibliography font inside Zotero?
faq.answer: Zotero's usage guide lists the document settings: citation style, language, footnote or endnote placement, Fields or Bookmarks, and MEDLINE abbreviations. It does not list a font setting. Check the font in Word itself, and test the fixes in this guide first.

faq.question: Does Track Changes cause the bibliography to look wrong?
faq.answer: Zotero's troubleshooting page says Track Changes may mark many or all citations as changed. It recommends turning the feature off. To turn it off, choose Review > Track Changes, clear it, then click Refresh in the Zotero toolbar.

faq.question: What does ⌥F9 do in Word for Mac?
faq.answer: ⌥F9 switches between field codes and field results. On compact keyboards, use fn+⌥F9. If the shortcut does not work, open Word > Preferences > View and uncheck Field codes instead of values. The shortcut toggles that same setting.

faq.question: Is Unlink Citations safe to use on a broken document?
faq.answer: No, not on your working copy. Zotero says removing field codes is irreversible. It should usually be done only in a final copy. Save a copy first, and treat Unlink Citations as the very last step.

faq.question: Should I use Fields or Bookmarks for citations?
faq.answer: Zotero's guide says to always choose Fields unless you need to collaborate with colleagues who use LibreOffice. Open Document Preferences from the Zotero toolbar in Word to see which one your document uses.

faq.question: Does the 22.8 percent error rate prove Zotero causes errors?
faq.answer: No. The 2013 study covered 125 master's theses and 3,564 references at Tamkang University. It counted reference errors. It did not test Zotero, and it did not measure formatting time. Use it as a reason to check your references, not as proof about the plugin.

faq.question: Will Lazur fix my bibliography for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides, points and explains. It answers out loud and can draft text. It does not click buttons, edit files or run other apps for you. You make each change yourself, with Lazur beside you.

faq.question: Is it safe to use an AI assistant with a thesis that has regulated data?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's or institution's rules first. Lazur sends audio and the screenshot to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Still, check the rules before you share a screen that holds client or patient data.

costs.title: Waiting time in the citation dialog
costs.text: A Zotero forum user on Zotero 7.0.29 and Word for Mac 16.103.1 reported about 35 seconds for one citation. The spinner sometimes never stopped. That is one report, not a measurement. Multiply it by every citation in a long paper and the waiting adds up.

costs.title: Reference errors you cannot see
costs.text: A 2013 study of 125 master's theses found a 22.8% error rate across 3,564 references. The study counted reference errors, not formatting time. It shows that citation mistakes are common enough to check before you submit.

costs.title: Lost work after a bad fix
costs.text: Unlink Citations cannot be undone, according to Zotero. A forum user reverted to saved versions each time a fix broke the document. Writers who never save a copy before testing pay the highest price.

costs.title: A rushed deadline
costs.text: A bibliography that breaks the night before submission forces a choice. You can restore an older copy and lose recent edits, or spend the evening on repairs. Both options cost more than a backup copy would.

causes.title: Track Changes marks citations as changed
causes.text: Zotero's troubleshooting page says Track Changes may mark many or all of the citations in your document as changed. It recommends turning the feature off. On rare occasions, it may make Zotero think a citation is corrupted, which can look like a formatting fault.

causes.title: Citations pasted into image captions
causes.text: Zotero's troubleshooting page says copied citations in image captions are most likely the source of the problem. A caption often arrives from another file or a web page. Check every caption before you run Refresh again.

causes.title: Clipboard tools on macOS
causes.text: Zotero's troubleshooting page says clipboard tools on macOS can interfere with the plugin. Text copied through a clipboard manager may carry formatting or hidden data. Paste as plain text when you can.

causes.title: Fields versus Bookmarks
causes.text: Zotero's guide says to always choose Fields unless you need to collaborate with LibreOffice users. A document set up another way is harder to repair when a citation breaks. Check Document Preferences first.

causes.title: A Zotero bug in your version
causes.text: A forum thread from late 2025 describes {Citation} placeholders after automatic updates were turned off. A Zotero staff member called it a bug tied to the Chicago style ID, with a fix in the beta. Compare your Zotero version with the current release.

causes.title: Field codes showing instead of results
causes.text: A citation can look wrong simply because Word shows field codes. Microsoft's Q&A answer says ⌥F9 toggles the view, and Word > Preferences > View controls the same setting. Check the view before you assume the citation is broken.

fixes.title: Save a copy before you start
fixes.text: Choose File > Save As and work only in the copy. Zotero advises testing in a copy of the document. If a fix fails, you still have the version that worked before you started.

fixes.title: Turn off Track Changes
fixes.text: Choose Review > Track Changes and clear it. Zotero recommends disabling Track Changes when citations break. Clearing old marks is a separate step, covered in the guide to accepting or rejecting tracked changes.

fixes.title: Correct the source item, then Refresh
fixes.text: Fix the wrong author, year or title in Zotero first. Then click Refresh in the Zotero toolbar in Word. Zotero's guide says Refresh updates all citations and the bibliography with changed item data.

fixes.title: Delete citations inside image captions
fixes.text: Search your captions for citation text and delete it. Retype any source you still need as plain text. Then click Refresh again. Zotero says captions are the most likely source of the problem.

fixes.title: Check field codes with ⌥F9
fixes.text: Press ⌥F9, or fn+⌥F9 on a compact keyboard, to see field codes. Press it again to switch back. If the shortcut fails, open Word > Preferences > View and uncheck Field codes instead of values.

fixes.title: Restart both apps
fixes.text: Quit Zotero and Word completely, then open them again. Zotero's troubleshooting steps start with this restart. Many forum threads report the restart as the only fix that helped.

fixes.title: Reinstall the Word plugin
fixes.text: Reinstall the Zotero plugin for Word, then restart Word. A 2018 Zotero staff reply advised the same step for Word 16.9 on Mac. The advice is old, but the test is cheap.

fixes.title: Isolate the broken section
fixes.text: In your copy, delete half the document, then test again. Keep the half that still fails. Repeat until the broken section is small. Zotero's troubleshooting page recommends this method for finding the failing part.

fixes.title: Unlink only on a final copy
fixes.text: Unlink Citations removes field codes and cannot be undone. Use it only on a final copy after you have finished editing. Zotero's guide says this is usually the right place for it.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.title: Back up and note the symptom
plan.text: Save a copy of the document and work only in that copy. Write down your Zotero version, your Word version and what the bibliography looks like. Under Zotero > About Zotero, check that you run Zotero 10 or the latest release.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.title: Clear the usual triggers
plan.text: Turn off Track Changes under Review > Track Changes. Search the image captions for citation text and delete it. Restart Zotero and Word, then click Refresh in the Zotero toolbar.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.title: Check field codes and the source items
plan.text: Press ⌥F9 to see field codes, then press it again to switch back. Fix any wrong author, year or title in Zotero, then click Refresh. Check the bibliography font in the copy after each step.

plan.label: Day 4
plan.title: Isolate, reinstall or ask for help
plan.text: If the problem remains, halve the document in your copy and test each half. Reinstall the Word plugin and restart Word. If nothing works, search the Zotero forum with your versions and your log.
